raw.assessment: The incumbent is plausibly adequate when course assignments remain stable: those 24 files had seven-minute median handling. Overall, however, 32/40 intended course sets and 17-minute median handling miss the targets. Assignment changes coincide with six affected exports, supporting investigation of week selection without establishing causality. The two renamed-course cases limit an assignment-only explanation. Short job runtimes and long replacement waits suggest additional service-process delay, but elapsed waiting is not measured coordinator handling. Zero observed cross-center rows is bounded evidence; the split-course center was absent.

openings.claim: Using present course metadata for a requested week may make exports sensitive to later assignment or naming changes, creating omissions or apparent omissions.
openings.delta: Test whether the incumbent preserves historical course identity and membership across metadata changes; distinguish missing records from labels coordinators cannot match.
openings.prediction: For fixed attendance and a fixed requested week, assignment or name changes alter exported membership or matching success; an unchanged control does not.
openings.probe: In fabricated staging, vary assignment and rename separately, compare participant/course membership and coordinator matching before and after, and include the omitted split-course condition plus another center. Keep the documented CSV and attendance entry active. Stop any proposed repair at the six-day and hosting limits.
assumptions: Staging can reproduce these metadata changes.
Historical reconstruction availability and repair effort remain unknown.

openings.claim: Does excess active handling primarily come from course-set reconciliation, or from download/import and replacement-request steps?
openings.delta: Locate the measured handling burden separately from replacement waiting before choosing the first change.
openings.prediction: A reconciliation bottleneck produces concentrated checking/correction time; a transfer or request bottleneck produces concentrated time in those steps, even with a correct course set.
openings.probe: Use the six coordinators' two short sessions with fabricated correct and affected CSVs. Time checking, correcting, downloading, importing, and requesting separately; record waiting separately. Retain only timing and issue categories within the private service or authorized workspace.
assumptions: Six coordinators cannot establish the next-40-export success rate.

raw.assessment: The sample misses the course-set and handling-time targets. Assignment changes and renames correlate with affected exports, but neither the selection failure nor the handling bottleneck is established. The unsampled course split leaves an important isolation and identity case untested.

openings.claim: A center-authorized, week-specific course manifest could preserve export membership through instructor changes and renames while attendance entry continues. The manifest would pin course identity and expected membership, not freeze attendance records.
openings.delta: Move the coordinator's course-set check before CSV generation and make its result independent of the current instructor assignment.
openings.prediction: With the same attendance records, changing only current assignment or display name will leave manifest-based membership stable. A fabricated course split will expose whether identity continuity requires an explicit coordinator decision.
openings.probe: In staging, compare current selection and a manifest prototype on unchanged, reassigned, renamed and split courses. Have consenting coordinators identify intended membership, then measure total preparation plus checking time. Keep the documented CSV, enforce center authorization during extraction, and exercise concurrent attendance entry.
assumptions: Stable course identifiers exist or are inexpensive to introduce.
Coordinators can resolve weekly membership without costly timetable reconciliation.
Implementation fits six engineer-days and existing hosting.

openings.claim: Would immediate, authorized replacement exports remove most excess coordinator handling, or would checking and spreadsheet work remain the dominant cost?
openings.delta: Distinguish delay in obtaining a replacement from active handling and from incorrect course selection; faster delivery alone need not improve the stated median.
openings.prediction: If request-and-return interruptions drive handling, immediate replacement will reduce active minutes and repeated checking. If spreadsheet work dominates, elapsed waiting will shrink while active minutes remain similar.
openings.probe: Use paired fabricated export tasks in the two coordinator sessions, counterbalancing ordinary replacement requests and simulated immediate delivery. Record active checking, requesting, downloading and importing separately from waiting. Deliver only the existing CSV inside authorized workspaces; assess measured savings before implementing a bounded, rate-limited regeneration control.
assumptions: Fabricated tasks approximate the relevant coordinator workflow.
Any subsequent implementation requires separate confirmation of six-day effort, hosting capacity and uninterrupted attendance entry.

critiques.assumption: Coordinator approval supplies reliable weekly membership cheaply.
critiques.limitation: D1-O6 establishes heterogeneous schedules; their completeness and timing are explicitly unmeasured. A manifest could stabilize an incorrect set or move reconciliation work upstream. This vulnerability is supported; actual manifest failure is unobserved.
critiques.opening: Assess unresolved weekly intent before requiring routine manifest approval.
critiques.comparison: Z1 diagnoses metadata sensitivity; A1 pins membership. Adding explicit unresolved identity decisions tests whether pinning has a trustworthy input.
critiques.probe: Proposed only: compare coordinator decisions with independently specified fabricated weekly intent, including stale schedules and a split. Count incorrect approvals and all preparation minutes.

critiques.assumption: Correct membership and immediate regeneration provide additive handling savings.
critiques.limitation: Faster regeneration could repeat a wrong selection; conversely, fixing selection could remove replacement demand. Neither interaction is established by job durations or waiting times.
critiques.opening: Measure the combined mechanism against both individual changes before implementing both.
critiques.comparison: A1 reduces selection-related rework; A2 reduces request/return friction. Their interaction is potentially substitutive: reliable initial exports leave little regeneration work to accelerate.
critiques.probe: Proposed only: cross original/corrected membership with ordinary/simulated-immediate delivery; time active work separately from waiting.

openings.claim: A minimal weekly membership resolver exposes uncertain identities before a manifest is trusted.
openings.delta: Demonstrate one authorized course-week decision with provenance and an explicit unresolved split state.
openings.prediction: Explicit uncertainty prevents some incorrect approvals but may increase preparation time.
openings.probe: Proposed fabricated task; score decisions and total handling against supplied scenario intent.
openings.fit: conditional on existing or affordable stable identifiers and dated intent evidence; retain D1-C1–C4 and original success measures
assumptions: Missing dependencies can be assessed within six engineer-days; otherwise stop before implementation.

openings.claim: Pinned membership plus authorized regeneration helps only where residual replacement work remains.
openings.delta: Compare combined treatment with each parent and incumbent.
openings.prediction: Combination adds little when membership repair eliminates replacements; unresolved intent makes both ineffective.
openings.probe: Proposed four short fabricated conditions across two sessions per coordinator; record preparation, checking and request effort. No world tests performed.
openings.fit: preserves original outcome, next-40-export targets and D1-C1–C4
assumptions: Session capacity permits four brief tasks; simulated delivery cannot establish real interruption savings.
